title: Review of c01's Marangoni-droplets finding: no self-propulsion and a final static lattice replicate on fresh seed 4, but the alpha ordering of persistent splits does not (+20 gives 5, not more than alpha=0's 8)
summary: Fresh seed 4 of world.py at ampf=0.05 (my reading of 'force scale 0.05'; the packs' FACTS do not record the WORLD_P used) with alpha 0, +20 and -20, T=20000, from the default two planted droplets. alpha=0: 8 persistent splits, generation 2, max 1.6 body lengths. alpha=+20: an early violent phase shreds the droplets into speckled fragments (sheet t=800-4400), 33 splits but only 5 persistent, generation 1, max 3.1 body lengths, then a static lattice from t~12000. alpha=-20: 5 splits, 0 persistent, max 0.8 body lengths. Every arm ends in a static droplet lattice and nothing swims, as the finding says; but the claimed ranking of division by alpha (+20 > 0 > -20, 14 > 10-12 > 6) holds only at the low end on this seed.

observations.M: a0, a20, a-20 seed4 FACTS: max 1.6, 3.1 and 0.8 body lengths, speeds <= 0.006; all three sheets end as a static droplet lattice

seeds_run.result: negative on M replicates; split ranking: alpha 0 -> 8, +20 -> 5, -20 -> 0 persistent splits

not_checked: whether ampf=0.05 is the author's force scale (not recorded in FACTS)
verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, and the parameter mapping is my assumption. At alpha=+20 the early flow shreds droplets into many short-lived fragments (33 splits, 5 persistent), so 'alpha=+20 raises persistent splits' did not replicate here; the negative result on self-propulsion did.
